Delete the Kankam’s statement that he was looking for a convenient place to stay, though there were only women there.
Delete the inserted picture of the close-up of Johnny dying, with blood flowing from his mouth.
Delete the statement of Sundari’s father that the doctor’s profession is not for doing service but for serving oneself.
When Sundari calls to ask the doctor to attend on her dying father, delete the reference to Emadharma Aspathri; and his asking her to get out and pushing her down.
Delete the picture of Thyagu stealing money from his parent's almirah.
After her father’s death, delete the picture and dialogue of Sundari shouting about money and observing that iron would have no heart.
Delete the explanation of Singa thevar of his ideal being to deprive the rich of their gold and distribute it to the poor.
Delete the father of Thyagu observing that even now Thyagu was getting trained to stealing and paying to Sundari and Hushila (consequential on Cut No. 3).
After the sword fight between Singathevar and VeeraSundari, delete her statement that stories buildings must topple down.
After she is crowned Veerasundari, in the third of her speeches, delete her statement that the occupation of these robbers was not theft but sacrifice.
Before Theni is engaged as a nurse, delete the sentence of compounder Ganapathi (with accompanying picture) “apparently she has contact with several places”.
Delete the picture of Veerasundari distributing robbed articles among slum dwellers.
When the police-inspector receives the letter sent by Banumathi, delete his referring to the public view of Veerasundari as a people’s benefactor.
While Banumathi invites the disguised Veerasundari to her bungalow, delete her statement “we exist only to help others”.
When Banumathi starts talking with Veerasundari, delete Sundari’s statement that Banumathi might be suffering from the troubles of youth (paruva baathai).

Delete the statement of Banumathi to the disguised Veeroaundari that in accordance with the classification into castes laid down by great people, she was a prostitute and in all the sequences where the police-inspector refers to Banumathi, delete his description of her as a classy.
Delete the speech by the police-inspector about the ideals of the police force and his ordering the suspension of two policemen.
Delete the picture of Veerasundari distributing robbed articles among slum dwellers.
In the court-scene, delete the picture of Rangoon Radha flogging the spy (seven contact shots plus two contact shots five sequences later).
Reduce considerably the fight sequences where Veerasundari and Kuttaj overcome the other robbers.

During the fight between Veerail un/lari and the imposter disguised as a beggar in the case, delete the sequences where they wrestle and roll about and throw each other down and box. (There is no objection to fighting with weapons between the man and the woman).

In the money lenders’ shop, delete the conversation between the salt and his accountant about the former standing for election, the reference to the opponents defeating him, the salt’s plan regarding the ballot-box and the expenditure, the proposal to put out Rs. 10 to make it 1,00,000 etc. (upto and including Kaisa-tiaisa-Naisa).

In the sequence regarding the boat, delete (a) at the beginning the picture of the salt at the iron-safe counting currency coins; (b) the conversation between the salt and Angamuthu regarding the dead girl who was not 18 years old but only 11 years old; (c) the statement of the salt that money is God; (d) Angamuthu’s reference to her having nine girls and her description of one of them as a cinema star, 18 years old and well-built, the offer of the salt to go to her, and his paying money to Angamuthu as advance; (e) after the plan to take a film in the salt’s house is mentioned delete Angamuthu relating the story of the proposed film and the proposed action of beating, kicking, and robbing, tying up etc. and the salt’s suggestion that if he was to be tied-up it might be by Sundari’s hands (the only portion not objected to are the bare mention of a plan to take a film in the salt’s house with the comment that it will all be acting and nothing more).
Where Veerasundari is taken by the salt to his iron-safe, delete the picture of Veerasundari in close-up, the camera focussed on her emphasised bust, (upto and including her going out to dance).

In the sequence in the salt’s house where the filming is supposed to take place delete (a) the rehearsal of beating on the head, by the director; (b) Veerasundari’s speeches about the salt’s business methods; (c) the salt being tied-up, beating first by Sundari and then by all, leaving only a suggestion at the end of the robbers leaving the house, the salt being shown tied-up.

At the beginning, delete the entire picture and dialogue showing the salt tied-up, the accountant coming and untying him, the safe being found empty and his weeping, the accountant asking under which account this loss should be entered, the salt sending him to the police (upto and including the exclamation Jftgat Ham).
Delete the picture of Veerasundan distributing the robbed articles among slum dwellers (there is no objection to her parting with her dupatta to a poor boy sitting there).

In the court-scene, delete (a) Veerasundari being given a book to hold; and being sworn as a witness, the book being taken from her thereafter; (b) during the defence advocate’s arguments, delete the insert picture and words of Sundari the accused referring to (1) her crime against the jeweller Naidu and (2) her crime against dead Banumathi and (c) in the judge’s summing up to the jury, his sentence that the actions of Sundari would appear to be proper.
